chunks: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no objection to the traveler calling the adhan while he is riding, and calling the iqamah while he is standing on the ground."
ai.seo_question: Can a traveler call the adhan while riding?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical concessions (rukhas) granted to travelers, distinguishing between the adhan, which may be performed while mounted due to its voluntary nature in travel, and the iqamah, which requires standing to maintain the dignity of the prayer's commencement. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing ease with ritual propriety, as recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*. It underscores the flexibility in fiqh that accommodates the physical realities of travel without compromising the structural integrity of the prayer ritual.
